A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LIMIT and embedding-capacity study. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, allowing the substantial theoretical revision and relocated material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original free-embedding optimization, LIMIT evaluations, fine-tuning experiments, qrel-pattern ablations, and dataset graph analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original optimization and retrieval results and adds a LIMIT-small synonym evaluation in Section 5.2 and Figure 6.

M1.justification: The retrieval models and free-embedding optimization procedure remain unchanged: Adam, InfoNCE, and unit-vector normalization are retained. Describing normalization as projected gradient descent does not establish a procedural change. Appendix C discusses other researchers' sigmoid-loss findings without introducing an implemented method.

E1.justification: v2 adds LIMIT-small with corpus attributes replaced by synonyms, introducing retrieval with reduced lexical overlap within the existing synthetic preference task. The random, cycle, and disjoint qrel variants disappear with their ablation. Standard full/small LIMIT and the external-dataset qrel analyses remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding retained experiments use the same comparison methods. The synonym panel reuses existing models, including GTE-ModernColBERT under the shortened GTE-ColBERT label. Newly cited methods such as Reason-ModernColBERT and Hypencoder are discussed without reported evaluations.

E3.justification: v2 adds synonym substitution followed by evaluation against the original LIMIT-small condition, and removes the controlled comparison of four qrel-generation patterns. Retained experiments preserve corpus/query counts, embedding-dimension sweeps, optimization stopping rules, and fine-tuning budgets. The new margin parameter belongs to the theorem, not a documented change to training.

E4.justification: v1's Section 5.4, Figure 6, and Table 3 test whether qrel connectivity explains difficulty; this entire ablation is removed. v2 instead adds a lexical-overlap robustness analysis showing how synonym substitution changes model performance. These address substantially different explanatory questions. The domain-shift experiment remains, and the BEIR correlation analysis moves to Appendix D.4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports explicit seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for these experiments. The new synonym results use the existing point-estimate reporting practice, and the polynomial fit's reported R-squared remains unchanged.

E6.justification: All matched numerical tables retain their values, but the qrel-pattern results are removed and a substantively different finding is added. v2 Figure 6 reports synonym-condition Recall@2 of 10.6 for BM25 and 25.6 for GTE-ColBERT, versus 97.8 and 83.5 on original LIMIT-small; BM25 consequently falls below most tested neural models. These compare different input conditions, not improved or degraded same-setting performance. Table 1 also adds numerical instances of the new theoretical bound.

T1.justification: v2 adds a unit-norm, positive-margin definition and Theorem 1, proving d ≥ log binom(n,k)/log(1+1/γ) through sphere packing, with asymptotic consequences. The original sign-rank definitions and proofs are retained in Appendix D rather than deleted. That appendix newly explains the k-dependent no-margin bound and its normalization and precision qualifications.

C1.justification: The three headline contributions—dimensional limitations, free-embedding experiments, and LIMIT—remain. However, v2's introduction removes the explicit attribution of state-of-the-art LIMIT failures to 'the theoretical underpinnings.' The broad abstract and conclusion claims otherwise persist despite the substantially revised formal assumptions.

C2.justification: v2 substantially revises the explanation of the limitation: Appendix D distinguishes the k-dependent margin-free result from the new margin-dependent bound, and Appendix C introduces learnability and loss-function qualifications. Section 5.2 adds evidence-based qualifications of BM25's lexical advantage and discusses architectural weaknesses beyond dimensional capacity. The alternatives discussion also allows more expressive similarity functions and future single-vector approaches.

D1.justification: v2 documents how Gemini 2.5 Pro generated synonym replacements, including avoiding collisions with existing items and using scientific names, similar meanings, or hypernyms. It also acknowledges remaining lexical overlap. The existing learning rate, epochs, sampling, hardware, inference framework, and code/data access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The main theoretical positioning shifts from communication complexity and sign-rank to sphere packing, Johnson–Lindenstrauss, and margin-based capacity arguments. New discussions of Alon et al. (1985), Bangachev et al. (2025), and related sigmoid-bottleneck work qualify the original argument. Several earlier sign-rank references disappear; this is a substantive repositioning rather than a bibliography-format change.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: the original theoretical development moves to Appendix D, the BEIR discussion moves to D.4, and the domain-shift subsection is folded into Section 5.2. Theoretical related work and implications are rewritten, new appendix sections are introduced, and language is edited throughout.

P2.justification: The document is reformatted from the DeepMind template to the ICLR layout, changing the title/abstract presentation, text width, typography, table scaling, and float placement. v2 adds the dimension-bound table and synonym bar chart, removes the qrel-pattern plot and table, and relocates the BEIR scatter plot to the appendix.

improvement.justification: The decisive gain is a more defensible theoretical foundation: v2 explicitly acknowledges the k-dependent no-margin bound and supplies a proved corpus-size-dependent bound under stated margin assumptions, addressing an important gap in v1's theoretical interpretation. The synonym experiment also provides a useful check on BM25's apparent advantage. These gains outweigh the loss of the qrel-pattern ablation, although broad claims equating optimization failure with representational impossibility remain insufficiently qualified.
